html:
Finland is a Nordic country of forests and lakes between Sweden and Russia. It was part of Sweden for some six hundred years, then from 1809 the Grand Duchy of Finland under the Russian tsar, with its own laws and parliament. In 1906 it gave women the vote, the first country in Europe to do so.

It declared independence in December 1917, after the Russian Revolution, and a short, bitter civil war between Reds and Whites followed in 1918. On the map it appears from 1920.

In the Winter War of 1939 to 1940 Finland held off a Soviet invasion but lost Karelia. It fought again alongside Germany from 1941 to 1944. Afterwards it stayed independent and democratic by keeping on careful terms with the Soviet Union. It joined the European Union in 1995, and NATO in 2023 after Russia's full invasion of Ukraine.
